Krasnik Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kraśnik, Poland

Demolished. This was Kraśnik's second Jewish cemetery, opened in the 1640s or 1650s specifically to replace the town's oldest cemetery when the synagogue complex relocated — closing the loop on that earlier site's own account of a forced 17th-century move. It remained in use until the early 19th century, when it was closed for sanitary reasons after residential housing grew up around it. The cemetery was destroyed during WWII; postwar redevelopment lowered the site by about a meter in the 1970s and turned it into a mix of a marketplace, parking lot, and built-up area. A dozen matzevah fragments were excavated nearby during a 1980s street renovation and are now preserved in the beit midrash building — a rare surviving physical trace.
